statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is LOW while macro Stress remains extreme.

headline: Two-sided overnight NQ keeps Tail low while oil, yields and today's data cluster keep Stress extreme
body: Delayed NQ is 29,485.50, down 0.09% from the prior close after trading 29,434.75-29,520.50. The recovery from the overnight low leaves price inside the range rather than pinned at an extreme. Brent above $91 and a U.S. 10-year yield near 4.78% keep the macro backdrop stressed.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 clock-hours, Tail ranged from 19% to 26%. The only elevated slot was 08:00 UTC on August 31; most later slots were WATCH, and Tail ended LOW at 04:00 UTC. Stress remained extreme at 97-99%, while the dominant mode shifted from event/whipsaw to mixed.
outlookSummary: Current Tail is LOW at 19% because overnight NQ has recovered from its low and remains inside the overnight range. Conditional Tail rises into WATCH around the Europe/U.S. handoffs and peaks at 24% around Barr, the cash open and the 14:00 UTC data cluster; higher bands still require persistent one-way structure.

forecast.analysis: At the Europe handoff, Tail is conditionally WATCH: acceptance outside the overnight range with shallow retracements would matter, while rejection back through the range would preserve two-sided structure.
European-opening flow could lift directional efficiency if the overnight range breaks and pullbacks stay shallow; rotation back through the range would keep the regime mixed.
Early-Europe continuation would require repeated extension after failed retracements to sustain WATCH; ordinary back-and-fill would argue against a persistent one-way path.
By mid-Europe, Tail would ease if price repeatedly overlaps prior ranges. A session-extreme hold alongside rising yields or oil would be the main condition for renewed concern.

forecast.analysis: Late-Europe structure remains conditional: meaningful pullbacks would keep Tail near the low/watch boundary, while clean extension without retracement would raise the next U.S. handoff risk.
As U.S. pre-market participation grows, failed retracements and repeated extension would be the principal Tail amplifiers; orderly two-sided trade would keep the regime mixed.
Pre-open positioning may become less stable ahead of Barr and the 14:00 UTC data cluster. Tail remains below block territory unless a directional impulse persists into deeper U.S. liquidity.
Barr's 13:05 UTC remarks and the 13:30 UTC cash open create a concentrated checkpoint. A one-way opening auction with shallow pullbacks would raise Tail; reversal or range repair would contain it.

JOLTS, ISM Manufacturing and Construction Spending arrive at 14:00 UTC. Surprise magnitude primarily raises Stress; Tail would require observed post-release continuation, failed retracements or extreme-holding.
In the first post-release hour, the key distinction is price discovery versus directional lock-in. Retracements and fading volatility would reduce Tail; repeated extension would keep WATCH elevated.
If the initial U.S. reaction develops meaningful counter-moves, Tail would ease toward the middle of WATCH. A delayed second directional leg remains the main contrary checkpoint.
U.S. midday usually provides a cleaner test of persistence: broad range overlap would lower path risk, while holding near a session extreme with weak retracement would keep WATCH active.
Into the afternoon, Tail would stay near the watch boundary if earlier event moves have been retraced. Renewed extension from an already stretched extreme would be the adverse conditional path.
Power-hour flow can re-accelerate a directional day. Tail would rise if late-session extension follows failed pullbacks; two-sided closing flow would keep the regime below block thresholds.
After the cash close, conditional Tail should ease if the session ends with meaningful range repair. An unresolved close near an extreme would keep overnight gap and continuation risk elevated.

During the daily futures maintenance interval, live price-path evidence is limited. Tail is therefore low absent a new discontinuity, while macro headline risk remains the main residual stress source.
At the Globex reopen, gap size and immediate retracement quality become the first overnight checkpoints. A contained reopen would support mixed structure; a one-way gap would raise WATCH risk.
During the early-Asia handoff, cross-market confirmation matters mainly if NQ itself becomes directionally efficient. Mixed regional signals would favor a contained WATCH assessment.
If early Asia remains inside the post-U.S. range, Tail would return to LOW. A fresh break with shallow pullbacks would be the condition for moving back to WATCH.
Mid-Asia risk stays low if rotations continue across prior levels. Persistent extension without meaningful mean reversion would invalidate that lower-Tail path.
Late-Asia trade would remain LOW under overlapping ranges and stable cross-assets; a geopolitical discontinuity or aligned rates/oil shock could quickly reopen Tail risk.

forecast.analysis: Ahead of the next European handoff, Tail remains low if overnight structure is balanced. A directional build near an overnight extreme would be the main pre-Europe warning condition.

The next Europe pre-open returns Tail to WATCH conditionally because a range break can gain liquidity. Confirmation would require persistent extension; immediate rejection would favor two-sided trade.
